claims.source_quote_ar: ولا يجوز قراءة القرآن بالعجمية  مطلقا
claims.claim_ar: لا يجوز قراءة القرآن بالعجمية مطلقًا.
claims.claim_en: It is not permissible to recite the Qur'an in a non-Arabic language (al-ʿajamiyya) at all.

claims.source_quote_ar: وجه المنع : أنه يذهب إعجازه المقصود منه
claims.claim_ar: سبب المنع أن القراءة بالعجمية تُذهب الإعجاز المقصود للقرآن.
claims.claim_en: The stated reason for the prohibition is that reciting in a foreign language removes the intended miraculousness (iʿjāz) of the Qur'an.

claims.source_quote_ar: وعن أبي حنيفة أنه يجوز مطلقا ، وعن أبي يوسف ومحمد : لمن لا يحسن العربية
claims.claim_ar: في الخلاف: عن أبي حنيفة جواز القراءة بالعجمية مطلقًا، وعن أبي يوسف ومحمد جوازها لمن لا يحسن العربية.
claims.claim_en: There is a scholarly disagreement: Abu Hanifa permits reciting the Qur'an in a non-Arabic language outright, while Abu Yusuf and Muhammad permit it only for those who do not know Arabic.
Reading the Qur'an using anomalous (shadhdh) readings is not permissible.
claims.needs_review_reason: The source asserts prohibition but immediately notes reports of consensus and an exception mentioned by al-Mawhub al-Jazri (possible allowance outside prayer), so the rule may have contextual exceptions and should be reviewed.

warnings: The provided source chunks discuss rules about recitation (prohibition of non-Arabic recitation, prohibition of shadh readings, reported scholarly disagreement) but do not contain explicit إِعْراب statements (مثل: مبتدأ، خبر، فاعل، مفعول به، حال، نعت) for the specific words of this ayah. Extracted claims therefore concern recitation rules and semantic effects linked to the word الْأَعْجَمِينَ (word 5) and a general rule about anomalous readings tied to the verb (word 2).

Some source statements present nuances or reported exceptions (e.g., mention of al-Mawhub al-Jazri permitting non-Arabic reading in non-prayer contexts, and reported differences among jurists). Those nuances may affect applicability; see needs_review_reason for the relevant claim.
